text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American inventor ROBERT FULTON was born in 1765. He built the first commercial steamboat, the 'Clermont' and invented the submarine.
French painter CLAUDE MONET, who was one of the pioneers of Impressionism, was born in 1840.

Australia's "Lemon-Syrup Poisoner" GEORGE DEAN was born in 1867. He was initially convicted for attempting to poison his wife, but was pardoned after an appeal. He then confessed and was jailed for perjury.

Australian author and screenwriter ARTHUR HOEY DAVIS, who wrote under the name STEELE RUDD, was born in 1868. His works include "On Our Selection" which featured country life with the farming family of "Dad RUDD". There were "Dad and Dave" books, films and radio shows.
Australian tennis star Sir NORMAN BROOKS was born in 1887. The left-handed player won the singles, doubles and mixed doubles at Wimbledon in 1907. He was nicknamed 'The Wizard'.
The first Prime Minister of independent India JAWAHARLAL NEHRU was born in 1889.
American senator JOSEPH McCARTHY, who led the Senate inquiry into alleged communists in the 1950s, was born in 1908.
American drummer with 'Angel' BARRY BRANDT was born in 1951.
** EVENTS **
1689 : English actress and favourite mistress of KING
CHARLES II of England, NELL GWYNN died. She had two children by the King.
1770 : Scottish explorer James Bruce discovered the
source of the Blue Nile on Lake Tana in northwest Ethiopia.
1896 : A new Highway Act declared it was no longer
necessary for a man to walk of a vehicle waving a red flag and the speed limit was raised from four to 14 kilometres an hour.
1900 : The existence of three different blood groups was
announced by the Pathological and Anatomical Institute in Vienna.
1910 : Captain EUGENE ELY, in a Curtiss biplane, made the
first takeoff from the deck of a ship. He took off from the light cruiser Birmingham, anchored in Hampton Roads, Virginia.
1940 : Coventry was blitzed by the Luftwaffe in a raid
which killed more than 500 people and almost completely destroyed the city's medieval cathedral.
1941 : The British aircraft carrier Ark Royal was sunk in
a German submarine attack off Gibraltar.
1948 : Prince CHARLES was born. The first child of
Princess Elizabeth and the Duke of Edinburgh was named CHARLES PHILIP ARTHUR GEORGE. A name which his future wife DIANA SPENCER couldn't quite master during the wedding ceremony.
1952 : Britain's first pop chart was published in the
"New Musical Express". The first number one was AL MARTINO's "Here In My Heart", followed by JO STAFFORD's "You Belong To My Heart" and NAT 'KING' COLE's "Somewhere Along The Way".
1973 : Princess ANNE married Captain MARK PHILLIPS in a

full military ceremony at Westminster Abbey. Both the bride and groom were world-class riders, she a European gold medallist and he an Olympic rider. The couple had two children and have divorced. Princess ANNE has remarried.
1983 : The world's biggest airport opened in Riyadh,
Saudi Arabia. The 3,864 million dollar airport covered 220 square kilometres of desert. It also had the world's tallest control tower at 74 metres high.
1989 : During a visit to Poland West German chancellor
HELMUT KOHL visited the death camp of Auschwitz.
1990 : In New Zealand a gunman killed 11 of the 50
inhabitants of Aramoana, near Dunedin in the South Island.
1994 : The first fare-paying passengers on the new rail
service travelled through the Channel Tunnel linking England and France.
1995 : Tens of thousands of Romanians packed central
Bucharest to mourn opposition leader and former political prisoner Corneliu Coposu, whose fight against communism broke his health but never won him power.
